bihar_raw_news.title: "We will not allow poison of casteism to prevail": Bihar minister Vijay Kumar Sinha
bihar_raw_news.content: "We will not allow poison of casteism to prevail": Bihar minister Vijay Kumar Sinha ANI | Updated: Nov 08, 2026 17:13 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel Patna (Bihar) [India], November 8 (ANI): Bihar Minister Vijay Kumar Sinha on Sunday called for unity beyond caste divisions, saying followers of the Sanatan tradition would not allow casteism to divide society. Referring to Prime Minister Narendra Modi's vision of "Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas", Sinha alleged that some people posing as intellectuals were attempting to mislead the youth and create chaos in the country. "The Prime Minister of our country envisions a path of Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas. However, there are those—enemies of the nation—who seek to sow chaos. Posing as intellectuals, they attempt to mislead the youth and deceive the people of this country. It is time for the children of India to not only become aware of such mindsets but also to cultivate a spirit that places the nation above all else. We, the followers of the Sanatan tradition, shall not be divided along the lines of caste; we will not allow the poison of casteism to prevail," he said. Meanwhile, Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary on Sunday announced that the state government will launch a campaign starting December 1 to encourage those who wish to willingly contribute toward the electricity subsidy. Speaking to the reporters, Choudhary extended his heartfelt Diwali greetings and best wishes to the people of the state, expressing hope that Bihar will march forward on the path of prosperity with greater strength. He emphasised the impact of the free electricity scheme, noting that it is illuminating homes across the state. Under this program, 1.92 crore families, spanning diverse economic backgrounds, are receiving 125 units of free electricity, with the government providing approximately Rs 10,000 annually in electricity subsidies per family. "I extend my heartfelt Diwali greetings and best wishes to the people of Bihar. I hope Bihar moves forward on the path of prosperity with greater strength. Under the NDA government's free electricity scheme, lamps are being lit in the homes of poor families. In fact, 1.92 crore families, whether rich or poor, are receiving 125 units of free electricity. We have also made an appeal regarding voluntary contributions. From December 1, we will launch a campaign encouraging those who wish to voluntarily contribute towards the electricity subsidy. Just as the Prime Minister appealed to people to voluntarily give up their LPG subsidies, we are making a similar appeal. The government provides electricity subsidies worth approximately Rs 10,000 annually to each family," he said. (ANI)

bihar_raw_news.title: From horse race to feast for 4 lakh: Bihar MLA Anant Singh's daughter's wedding plans
bihar_raw_news.content: SIGN IN Edition IN IN US Download App Follow Us On: News India From horse race to feast for 4 lakh: Anant Singh’s daughter’s wedding plans From horse race to feast for 4 lakh: Bihar MLA Anant Singh's daughter's wedding plans Shivangi Singh will marry Rishikesh Kumar, also known as Ankit, a resident of Krishnanagar in Patna's Bihta, on November 25. Advertisement The celebrations come less than a week before the Mokama MLA is due to surrender on December 1 under a court order. By: India Today News Desk Patna , Nov 8, 2026 16:11 IST Last Updated Nov 8, 2026 16:11 IST Published by Aprameya Rao Nov 8, 2026 15:58 IST Edited by Aprameya Rao A feast for four lakh people, flowers from abroad and a horse race with a Mahindra Thar for the winner. In Bihar’s Ladma village, several acres are being readied for Mokama MLA Anant Singh’s younger daughter’s wedding, with politicians, actors and singers on the invitation list. Shivangi Singh will marry Rishikesh Kumar, also known as Ankit, on November 25. The family will also hold the sacred-thread ceremony of Singh’s younger son, Abhinav, that day. advertisement ❮ ❯ Read Full Story The celebrations fall less than a week before Singh’s court-ordered surrender on December 1 in the Dular Chand Yadav murder case. He is accused of orchestrating the killing of Yadav, who was campaigning for a rival candidate in Mokama in October 2025. Singh, recently expelled from the JD(U), had been granted bail by the Patna High Court in March. Decorators from Mau in Uttar Pradesh have been brought in to put up elaborate pandals, while a separate ground is being prepared for the horse race. Horses are expected to arrive in Barh from across the country over the next few days. The race winner will receive a Mahindra Thar, while the runner-up will take home a motorcycle, Singh said. There will be no firecrackers, he added, saying environmental concerns would be kept in mind. Singh said he plans to invite Prime Minister Narendra Modi. Former Bihar chief minister Nitish Kumar, RJD chief Lalu Prasad Yadav and Leader of Opposition Tejashwi Yadav are also among the political invitees. Actor Sonu Sood, folk singer Maithili Thakur, MP and singer Manoj Tiwari, Bhojpuri star Pawan Singh and actress Akshara Singh have been invited, along with other Bollywood personalities. Their attendance is yet to be confirmed. A stage programme featuring Bhojpuri, Magahi and Mumbai-based performers is planned. Singh’s wife, Neelam Devi, has offered wedding invitations to deities as part of the customary rituals ahead of the celebrations. - Ends IN THIS STORY # Bihar

bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar to launch drive from Dec 1 to encourage 'well-off' people to surrender power subsidy
bihar_raw_news.content: Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary distributes sweets among people during Deepotsav celebrations on the occasion of Diwali in Patna, Bihar, Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. (Photo | PTI) Bihar Bihar to launch drive from Dec 1 to encourage 'well-off' people to surrender power subsidy He said the government provides electricity subsidies worth around Rs 10,000 annually to each family and added that those who voluntarily surrender the benefit would be recognised for their contribution. TNIE online desk Updated: 8th Nov, 2026 at 5:40 PM Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary on Sunday reiterated his appeal to financially well-off families and income tax payers to voluntarily give up the benefit of 125 units of free electricity, saying the state government would launch a campaign from December 1 to encourage them to do so. Choudhary made the announcement while interacting with reporters during his visit to slum areas in Patna to celebrate Diwali with underprivileged sections of society. He also distributed sweets among residents on the occasion. Addressing a youth parliament in Patna last week, the chief minister said the state government was spending around Rs 23,000 crore annually on electricity subsidies and appealed to affluent families to voluntarily give up the benefit of 125 units of free power to help the state utilise resources for development. "Under this campaign, people will be encouraged to voluntarily give up subsidy benefits. Just as Prime Minister Narendra Modi had appealed to people to surrender their LPG subsidies, we are making a similar appeal," Choudhary told reporters. He said the government provides electricity subsidies worth around Rs 10,000 annually to each family. Those who voluntarily surrender the benefit would be recognised for their contribution, he added. The chief minister also said he had appealed to public representatives and administrative officials to visit tribal areas and meet members of Dalit and other extremely backward communities to celebrate Diwali with them. "Officials should share both their joys and sorrows and become a part of their lives. Festivals should be celebrated by everyone, and nobody should be left out. That is why I have come here personally as well," he said. Choudhary also praised Modi for celebrating Diwali with security personnel in Bastar. "PM Modi has often stood alongside soldiers at the borders, and today, under his leadership, the country has become Naxal-free. It is significant that Modi himself is visiting a place like Bastar and celebrating Diwali there with our security personnel," he said. The chief minister further said Modi would visit Bihar on November 21 and was expected to announce several development and infrastructure projects. bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar Announces 83-km Ganga Riverfront Road Between Munger and Bhagalpur
bihar_raw_news.content: Home Breaking News Bihar Announces 83-km Ganga Riverfront Road Between Munger and Bhagalpur Breaking News Bihar Announces 83-km Ganga Riverfront Road Between Munger and Bhagalpur By Tenzin Choden November 8, 2026 0 Copy URL Facebook Linkedin X WhatsApp Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary has announced that work will begin on an approximately 83-km Ganga riverfront road between Munger and Bhagalpur, linking the project to improved regional transport and development opportunities along the river corridor. Choudhary made the announcement while inaugurating the Munger Deepotsav programme at the Shri Shri 108 Badi Durga Maharani Mandir in Kalyanpur, under Bariarpur block of Munger district, on Saturday. The event, organised by Youth Club Kalyanpur on the eve of Diwali, featured the simultaneous lighting of 11,11,111 lamps. According to the report, the chief minister said the proposed road would improve transport facilities in the region and open up new possibilities for development. The announcement did not provide details on the project’s estimated cost, alignment, land requirement, executing agency, construction schedule or funding structure. The road proposal was presented in the context of the challenges faced by settlements and farmers along the Ganga. Choudhary referred to recurring floods and crop losses, saying that water from the Nepal Tarai region and the Sone river merges into the Ganga around Dussehra and contributes to flooding in several areas. He said better management and use of Ganga water would be important for farmers. The chief minister also referred to an agreement signed on November 2 with Union road transport and highways minister Nitin Gadkari, although the report does not specify whether that agreement directly covers the announced riverfront road, its financing, flood-control works or another water-management intervention. The proposed road would connect two important urban centres in eastern Bihar, but its practical impact will depend on how the alignment is designed and how it interacts with flood-prone areas, agricultural land and existing road infrastructure. No technical details about bridges, embankments, drainage systems or flood-resilient construction standards were provided in the announcement. The chief minister made the infrastructure announcement alongside a broader statement on employment and economic development. He said the state government was working towards creating a system by 2030 in which people from Bihar would not be forced to migrate outside the state for work. He said the government aimed to expand opportunities for jobs, business and self-employment within Bihar. The Munger Deepotsav programme itself was described as a historic celebration for Bihar, with more than 11 lakh lamps lit at one location. Before attending the event, Choudhary offered prayers and performed puja at the Badi Durga Maharani Mandir. The next formal milestones for the Ganga riverfront road will be the release of its alignment, project cost, implementing authority, land and environmental requirements, and construction timeline. The supplied report does not state when physical work is expected to begin beyond the chief minister’s announcement that it will start. national_raw_news.title: PM Modi celebrates Diwali with security personnel in Chhattisgarh’s Bastar
national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi today celebrated Diwali with the brave security personnel in Bastar, Chhattisgarh. Addressing the security personnel, Mr Modi said that this Diwali is special as the country has won its decades-long battle against Naxalism and Maoist terror. He said, for the first time, every district in the country is free from Naxalism and crores of citizens have now overcome the fear of Left Wing Extremism. Mr Modi described it as an extraordinary achievement and credited millions of brave security personnel for their contribution. Prime Minister recalled that, at one point, more than 230 districts across nearly 20 states were affected by Naxalism. He said that large parts of the country, including Bihar, Maharashtra, Odisha, Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh and Chhattisgarh, were affected by this menace. Mr Modi highlighted that between 2004 and 2013, the number of security personnel martyred every year was higher than the number of Naxalites killed. He said that the governments at the time treated Naxalism as an incurable disease and failed to address the issue. Mr Modi highlighted for the first time in 47 years, not a single CRPF jawan has lost his life on duty in the past year. Prime Minister said, this is a victory for the country’s right policies and strong resolve. The Prime Minister said that security personnel have made countless sacrifices for the unity and integrity of the nation. He expressed gratitude to every personnel of the CRPF, CoBRA, BSF, ITBP, SSB, IRB, state police forces, Bastar Fighters and special forces, including women commandos, for their invaluable service to the nation. Mr Modi said that, guided by the spirit of service, the government has transformed the lives of people in Naxal-affected areas. He said that as a result of these efforts, even those who had suffered due to Naxalism came forward to extend their support to the government and security forces. The Prime Minister said when the country works with the spirit of Nation First, peace and security are ensured and the nation reaches new heights of development. Mr Modi said that over the past twelve years, the country has not only won the battle against Naxalism and separatism but has also made significant progress in the fight against poverty. He highlighted that, on the one hand, 50 crore people have been lifted out of extreme poverty, while, on the other hand, Naxal violence has come to an end in the country. The Prime Minister visited a security camp (Central Reserve Police Force) at Karanpur in Bastar.

national_raw_news.title: Benchmark indices surrender initial gains, close lower in special trading session 2 hours ago 37
national_raw_news.content: The Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) and National Stock Exchange (NSE) conducted muhurat trading on the occasion of Diwali, marking the beginning of Samvat 2083. Benchmark domestic equity indices failed to hold on to their initial gains and ended the day’s special trading session in the negative zone. The Sensex ended marginally lower by 29 points to close at 80 thousand 999, while the Nifty dipped 44 points, or 0.18 per cent to settle at 24 thousand 986. Conversely, the broader market on the National Stock Exchange ended with gains. The Midcap 100 index rose over 0.1 per cent, while the Smallcap 100 index jumped one per cent. In the Sensex pack, 16 out of 30 companies edged upward. Among the top gainers, SunPharma surged almost three per cent, Tata Steel added 1.9 per cent and Maruti advanced 0.8 per cent. In the top laggards, Mahindra and Mahindra dipped over 0.9 per cent, Indigo dropped 0.9 per cent and Trent fell 0.8 per cent. Among the Sectoral indices at the BSE, 18 out of 28 sectors ended in positive territory. Among the top gainers, Healthcare advanced over 1.6 per cent, Housing Finance rose 1.1 per cent and Industrials added one per cent. In contrast, Realty slipped half a per cent, top 10 banks, Private Banks, and Bankex dropped almost 0.3 per cent, while Consumer Durables lost 0.2 per cent. The overall market breadth at the BSE was positive, as shares of 3 thousand 253 companies advanced, 947 declined and 254 remained unchanged.

national_raw_news.content: The festival of light, Deepawali, is being celebrated with religious fervour and gaiety across the country and abroad. President Droupadi Murmu has extended Diwali greetings to Indians at home and abroad. In her message, she said the festival symbolises the victory of virtue over negativity and marks the end of suffering and the beginning of a joyful and prosperous life. The President has also urged people to protect the environment, promote harmony and contribute towards building a Viksit Bharat. She also wished every citizen good health, happiness and prosperity. Vice President C P Radhakrishnan has greeted fellow citizens and people across the world on the occasion of Diwali. In a social media post, Mr Radhakrishnan said, Diwali celebrates the universal triumph of light over darkness, good over evil and truth over falsehood, reminding people of the eternal ideal of Satyamev Jayate – Truth Alone Triumphs. He hoped that this Diwali will bring happiness, peace and prosperity to every home and strengthen the bonds of unity and harmony. Prime Minister Narendra Modi will continue his tradition of celebrating Diwali with the brave personnel of the Armed Forces. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has also greeted everyone on the occasion of Diwali. In a social media post this morning, the Prime Minister said, the festival symbolises resolve against darkness. Prime Minister Modi also shared a video message on social media. He said, the festival of lights illuminates the nation and reflects the resolve to overcome darkness. He wished everyone happiness, peace and prosperity.

national_raw_news.title: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh stresses highest operational readiness amid evolving security threats
national_raw_news.content: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh has urged the armed forces to maintain the highest level of operational readiness, stressing the need to strengthen domain awareness, cyber resilience and information integrity amid evolving security challenges. Addressing Indian Air Force (IAF) personnel at Air Force Station Bagdogra in West Bengal on the eve of Diwali, Mr Singh said, modern warfare has expanded beyond conventional border conflicts to include asymmetric warfare, proxy conflicts, cyberattacks, drone swarms and information operations. He cautioned that adversaries were increasingly exploiting vulnerabilities through misleading social media campaigns aimed at creating distrust among local communities and security personnel. The Defence Minister emphasised that military personnel must play a wider role in countering such threats by maintaining public trust and engaging with local communities. Referring to the Cabinet’s approval of the ‘Second Tour of Duty’ for Agniveers, the Defence Minister said the initiative would offer them another opportunity to serve the nation. He said all Agniveers would be eligible for enrolment as regular soldiers after completing their two-year engagement, subject to their willingness and prescribed selection criteria. Calling the decision a significant Diwali gift, the Defence Minister reiterated the government’s commitment to the welfare of defence personnel and their families. He also extended Diwali greetings to the Air Warriors and their families, acknowledging the sacrifices of personnel serving away from home during festivals and appreciating the support extended by their families. Chief of the Air Staff Air Chief Marshal Ashutosh Dixit, Air Officer Commanding of Air Force Station Bagdogra Air Commodore Manish Sharma and other senior IAF officials attended the event. Describing Bagdogra as a strategically important location for India’s security framework, particularly in the Northeast, Singh praised the Air Warriors for their dedication and said their preparedness was vital to regional stability. Highlighting the government’s push for ‘Aatmanirbhar Bharat’, Mr Singh acknowledged the contribution of Indian start-ups and industries to the development of drones, anti-drone systems and advanced military equipment. He urged the forces to embrace indigenous technologies and strengthen their capabilities in drone operations and cybersecurity.

national_raw_news.title: Petroleum Ministry says E20 petrol across India meets prescribed quality standards
national_raw_news.content: The Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas has reaffirmed the claim that E20 petrol supplied by public sector oil marketing companies (OMCs) across the country, including Karnataka, conforms to the prescribed quality standards. It noted that E20 petrol supplied by the three OMCs conforms to IS 17021, the Bureau of Indian Standards specification for ethanol-blended motor gasoline. The Ministry rejected the claims of Karnataka Government that fuel sold at certain retail outlets in the state contains excessive ethanol. The Ministry said that 893 samples collected across 27 States and Union Territories, including 56 from Karnataka, meet the prescribed specifications. The Ministry added that all 56 samples tested in Karnataka conform to IS 17021 specifications, with ethanol content ranging from 19 to 20 per cent. Earlier, the three oil marketing companies, Indian Oil Corporation, Bharat Petroleum Corporation and Hindustan Petroleum Corporation, had clarified that the claims, as reported, were not supported by tests conducted in accordance with the prescribed statutory and technical procedures. In view of the concerns raised, the three OMCs have requested the Karnataka Government to share the complete sampling documentation, outlet-wise laboratory reports and details of the test methodology adopted for the reported findings. The Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas said that the OMCs maintain established quality assurance systems across their supply and distribution networks to ensure that blended fuel meets the applicable BIS specifications before reaching consumers.

national_raw_news.title: Shyama Puja, also known as Kali Puja, celebrated across West Bengal with devotion
national_raw_news.content: In West Bengal, Shyama Puja, popularly known as Kali Puja, is being celebrated today across West Bengal and several parts of the country with traditional fervour and devotion. The festival coincides with Diwali in many parts of the country. From magnificent community pandals to age-old temples and household shrines, preparations are complete to welcome Goddess Shyama, the powerful manifestation of divine feminine energy. The festival is observed on the new moon night of the Hindu month of Kartik, following traditional rituals and religious customs. Some of Bengal’s most revered Kali temples are witnessing special arrangements for the occasion. The Dakshineswar Bhavatarini Temple, closely associated with the spiritual legacy of Sri Ramakrishna Paramahansa, the historic Kalighat Kali Temple, Tarapith and Adyapeath are among the major centres of attraction. Special puja arrangements have also been made at the ancestral home of saint-poet Ramprasad Sen in Halisahar, Karunamoyee Kalibari, Firingi Kalibari and Thanthania Kalibari in Kolkata. The historic Hanseswari Temple at Bansberia in Hooghly district, the famous Boro Maa Kali Puja in Naihati and the Kali temple at Kankalitala, one of the revered Shakti Peethas, are also preparing to receive large numbers of devotees. As Bengal celebrates the triumph of divine power over evil, the night of Amavasya is transformed into a celebration of light, faith and devotion.

national_raw_news.title: Global leaders and diplomats extend greetings on Diwali
national_raw_news.content: The festival of lights, Diwali, will be celebrated tomorrow, marking the triumph of good over evil. Ahead of the celebrations, wishes have begun pouring in from world leaders and diplomats across the globe, including those serving in India. UAE Vice President and Ruler of Dubai, Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, extended his Diwali greetings to people celebrating the festival in the United Arab Emirates and around the world. In a post on X, he wished that the festival of lights would bring peace, hope and goodness, while filling people’s lives with safety, happiness and prosperity. European Union Ambassador to India, Jean-Eric Paquet, recalled his first Diwali experience in the country. Sharing his thoughts on X, he described it as a beautiful experience, with lights illuminating every corner. The Embassy of the Republic of Korea in India organised a special diya-decoration workshop to mark the festivities. Norwegian Ambassador to India, May-Elin Stener, shared a video on X extending her Diwali wishes. She noted that although the celebrations were being held within the Embassy premises, the festive greetings and spirit extended far beyond its walls. Germany’s Ambassador to India and Bhutan also conveyed his wishes on the occasion. Denmark’s Ambassador to India, Rasmus Abildgaard Kristensen, highlighted the significance of the festival, saying that even the smallest light can make a big difference. The Embassy of Japan in India also joined the celebrations by hosting a festive lunch. Earlier, US President Donald Trump took part in a ceremonial diya-lighting event at the White House to mark Diwali. The celebration brought together prominent members of the Indian-American community. India’s Ambassador to the United States, Vinay Kwatra, was also present at the ceremony held in the Oval Office. In another significant development, governors of five US states celebrated Diwali at official venues for the first time. The celebrations, held in Idaho, Nebraska, Montana, North Dakota and Washington states.

national_raw_news.title: President, Prime Minister extend greetings on auspicious occasion of Diwali
national_raw_news.content: President Droupadi Murmu has extended her greetings to all Indians living in India and abroad on the eve of Diwali today. In a message, the President said that the festival of Diwali marks the victory of virtues over negative tendencies. She added that the festival also signifies the end of suffering and the beginning of a joyful and prosperous life. She said that on this occasion, people worship Lord Ganesh for auspicious beginnings and well-being, and Goddess Mahalakshmi for prosperity. President Murmu also wished for good health, happiness and prosperity of every citizen of the country. She also urged everyone preserves the environment, live with harmony. The President also appealed to the youth to contribute in building a Viksit Bharat. Prime Minister Narendra Modi also extended his greetings on the occassion of Diwali. Sharing a video message on social media, Mr Modi said that the festival of lights illuminates the entire country and reflects the resolve to overcome darkness. He wished that the festival and the times ahead bring happiness, peace and prosperity to everyone. The Prime Minister further said he celebrates Diwali with great enthusiasm and that, as in previous years, he would continue the tradition of celebrating the festival with the brave soldiers of the country. Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla has extended his greetings to the citizens for Deepavali, Govardhan Puja, and Bhai Dooj.
